patch_description: Key insight: with circle centers fixed, maximizing the sum of radii is a *linear program*: maximize Σr_i subject to r_i + r_j ≤ d_ij (pairwise) and r_i ≤ min border distance. The previous uniform-radius assignment (r = min over all constraints) massively underuses space — border and corner circles can be much larger than lattice circles. So I: (1) keep the hexagonal lattice as a starting layout, (2) solve the exact LP for optimal radii at those positions (scipy `linprog` with HiGHS — fast for 26 variables / ~350 constraints), and (3) run a hill-climb over centers: random jitter perturbations with a decreasing step size, re-solving the LP after each move and accepting improvements. Wall-constrained circles also get directed pushes away from walls. A tiny safety epsilon (1e-9) on all constraints plus a final 1-1e-6 radius shrink guarantees strict feasibility. A greedy fallback keeps the program working if scipy is unavailable.
